title: CoderHelm plugin manifest
description: The plugin.yaml file at the root of a CoderHelm plugin. A plugin is text plus approved tools: its behavior comes from its agents and skills, and this file declares what it may touch.

$schema.description: Optional. Point editors at this schema for completion and checks.

name.description: The plugin's id. Lowercase letters, digits and `-`, optionally namespaced by publisher as `publisher/name`.

version.description: The plugin's version, in semantic versioning (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`). Installs are pinned by content hash, so the version is a label for people; raise it whenever you publish.

description.description: One line saying what the plugin does. Shown in the catalog and on the plugin's page.

skills.description: Paths or globs of the plugin's skills, relative to the plugin's folder. Skills use the same SKILL.md format as skill repos and apply only to this plugin's runs.

agents.description: Paths or globs of the plugin's agents. Each agent file is Markdown with frontmatter; its body is the agent's instructions.

settings.description: Values each team fills in on the plugin's page. Values live with the team, never in the plugin.

tools.description: Every tool the plugin's agents may call. A tool that is not listed here does not exist for a plugin run.

triggers.description: What starts a run of the plugin, besides a person writing a brief on the plugin's page.

outputs.description: What a run produces. Drafts wait in the review queue; a publish output sends an approved draft out through a consequential tool.

budget.description: The plugin's own monthly token limit. The team can change it on the plugin's page, and the team's limits apply too.

monthly_tokens.description: Tokens the plugin may use per month. Empty or 0 means no limit of its own.

key.description: The setting's name. Lowercase letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter.

type.description: `string` is a value the team types. `secret` is sealed, never shown again once saved, and never given to a model. `connection` asks the team to connect an account.

provider.description: For a `connection`: how the account is connected, such as `oauth2`.

scopes.description: For an OAuth connection: the scopes asked for. Adding a scope in a new version waits for an admin.

sensitive.description: Keep the value out of every prompt and never send it back to the dashboard. `secret` and `connection` settings are always sensitive.

risk.description: `read` only looks. `write` changes something a person can still review, such as a draft in a CMS. `consequential` reaches people or money (publish, send, post) and runs only after an approval.

mcpTool.description: Tools from an MCP server the team has on its Connections page.

allow.description: Tool names, or `*` globs, from that server the plugin may call. Everything else on the server is hidden from the run.

risk.description: The highest risk among the allowed tools.

namedTool.description: A built-in CoderHelm tool, or a tool the plugin defines.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits and `_`. Agents call the tool by this name.

kind.description: `builtin` is one of CoderHelm's own tools, such as reading release notes. `http` is a tool the plugin defines that calls an outside service with the team's connection.

description.description: When an agent should use the tool.

manualTrigger.description: A person starts a run from the plugin's page by filling in a short form.

form.description: The form's fields: `text` for a box to write in, or a list of choices to pick from.

cron.description: Five-field cron: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.

releaseTrigger.description: Runs when a release is published on a GitHub repo the team connected. The run gets the release notes CoderHelm wrote.

kinds.description: The kinds of draft a run may save. `action` is a step to take, such as an update to a record, rather than something to read.

via.description: The name of a `consequential` tool from `tools` that sends an approved draft out.

role.description: Who should approve, as a short name such as `marketing_editor`. The team lists the actual approvers on the plugin's page.

min.description: How many different people must approve.

approval.description: The approval a draft needs before it is published. The person who asked for a draft never approves it.
